newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps ease back, bar firmer heavy fuel.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps ease back, bar firmer heavy fuel.

text.p: European oil swaps were a touch softer on Friday except for narrowly firmer fuel oil amid very quiet trading as the U.S. Independence holiday sucked interest and liquidity out of the market.

Brent CFDs were a couple of cents off, but nothing was heard traded. July 7-11 slipped to flat against August Brent compared with +4 cents on Thursday, while July 14-18 was hovering around -13 cents from -11/12 cents. July 21-25 was put at -15/16 cents, off two cents or so and July 28-August 1 was seen steady at -19 cents.
Heavy fuel was very narrowly firmer by 50 cents or so on July paper. Dealers said July was pegged at $84.50 with August bid at $84.50. In the Mediterranean $78 was done for July.
Low sulphur swaps were particularly dead.
"It's very much a U.S. driven market and the only driving the Americans are doing is in their cars visiting relatives (for the July 4 public holiday," said one European trader.
The high-low spread was steady with 4Q holding at $7.75.
Gasoline swaps eased off $1 or so with July slipping to $186.50 and August sliding to $185.50. Traders said the drop reflected crude's fall yesterday and thin trading on Friday.
"It certainly is quiet, but gasoline had to react to crude and it has by coming off $1," said one dealer.
Naphtha swaps eased back a touch by $1 or so on July to $175 but further out August held at $177.5 and September at $180.50. Traders said close in paper was reacting to crude.
